decisions.reason: Connects the top-level ESM import in plugin/lib/client.js to the host-boot classic-script combo: one parse error aborts the whole 53-entry script so zero entries register, and the browser-error name is explained as the first awaited innocent entry (@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-registry) while the real culprit file appears in the compile-error suffix. No claim that raw ESM is invalid everywhere.

Bisects the cordis.patch.yml insert rows and flags the offending bundle via a cheap static scan for top-level import/export tokens, confirmed by position 1:1. Describes the required window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory}) classic-script shell with package-name id, host React via require inside the factory, module.exports return, and inject/apply exports — matching the working-plugin excerpt.

Uses plugin-apply-error.txt to explain the parent entry owns the declaration and apply order is not guaranteed; shows the exact ctx.slots.inject('settings.section', () => ctx.slots.register(...)) deferred form; states registrants pass name/id/order/optional label and must not pass kind/scope, noting the user's call included the forbidden fields.

Grounded in host-boot-log.txt and restart-notes.txt: combo assembled once per boot, so edits and hard refresh change nothing until a full host stop/start; explains EADDRINUSE as an orphaned node process retaining the port, killed via taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F, then relaunch, refresh, and verify the plugin list.

Proposes per-bundle parse/ESM-token validation at startup or combo build with headline attribution to the failing plugin file rather than the first awaited entry. Authoring checklist covers the loader factory shell, host React via require and inject/apply, deferred cross-entry slot registration with correct fields, and full host restart with Windows process-tree cleanup.

caps.reason: The report consistently requires bundled classic-script packaging, the slots.inject deferred registration, registrant-supplied fields without kind/scope, and full host restarts; no affirmative advice endorses bare ESM, immediate cross-entry registration, declaration-owned fields on registrants, or HMR/browser-refresh-only iteration.
